name.text: Finding a missing frequency from the median

questiontext.text:
The table shows the lengths, in cm (to the nearest cm), of the fish landed at a beach in Homa Bay one morning.

Length (cm){@lo[1]@}–{@hi[1]@}{@lo[2]@}–{@hi[2]@}{@lo[3]@}–{@hi[3]@}{@lo[4]@}–{@hi[4]@}{@lo[5]@}–{@hi[5]@}{@lo[6]@}–{@hi[6]@}
Frequency (\(f\))[[if test="is(jx=1)"]]\(x\)[[else]]{@f[1]@}[[/if]][[if test="is(jx=2)"]]\(x\)[[else]]{@f[2]@}[[/if]][[if test="is(jx=3)"]]\(x\)[[else]]{@f[3]@}[[/if]][[if test="is(jx=4)"]]\(x\)[[else]]{@f[4]@}[[/if]][[if test="is(jx=5)"]]\(x\)[[else]]{@f[5]@}[[/if]][[if test="is(jx=6)"]]\(x\)[[else]]{@f[6]@}[[/if]]

The median length is \({@medd@}\) cm. Find \(x\).

\(x =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Work backwards through the median formula \(\text{median} = L + \dfrac{n/2 - CF}{F} \times c\). The median \({@medd@}\) cm lies in the class {@lo[km]@}–{@hi[km]@}, so \(L = {@exd(Lm)@}\), \(CF = {@CFm@}\), \(F = {@Fm@}\) and \(c = 10\). The unknown \(x\) comes after this class, so it changes \(n\) but not \(CF\) or \(F\): \(n = {@n0@} + x\).

\[{@medd@} = {@exd(Lm)@} + \frac{({@n0@} + x)/2 - {@CFm@} }{ {@Fm@} } \times 10\]so \(({@n0@} + x)/2 - {@CFm@} = ({@medd@} - {@exd(Lm)@}) \times {@Fm@} \div 10 = {@exd(half-CFm)@}\), giving \(({@n0@} + x)/2 = {@exd(half)@}\), \({@n0@} + x = {@exd(2*half)@}\) and \(x = {@xv@}\).

Check: with \(x = {@xv@}\), \(n = {@n@}\), and position \({@exd(n/2)@}\) does lie in the class {@lo[km]@}–{@hi[km]@}.

Statistics II: finding a missing frequency from the median

Grade 12 CBE Core and Essential 3.1: Use the grouped median formula backwards to find a missing frequency.

truefeedback.text: You placed the median at position \((n + 1)/2\). For grouped data use \(n/2\).

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(mchk>=0)"]]With \(x = {@ans1@}\) the median would be \({@dispdp(float(mchk),2)@}\) cm, not \({@medd@}\) cm. [[/if]]Write \(n = {@n0@} + x\), put the position \(n/2\) into the median formula and solve for \(x\).
